newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: CIS leaders call for end to Afghan fighting.
newsitem.headline: CIS leaders call for end to Afghan fighting.

text.p: The leaders of five former Soviet republics on Friday urged rival groups in Afghanistan to stop fighting and hold talks.
"We call upon all warring parties to stop hostilities and resume peace negotiations," Kazakhstan's President Nursultan Nazarbayev said at a joint news conference after a summit meeting.

Nazarbayev also accused the hardline Islamic Taleban militia of violating human rights after its seizure of the Afghan capital Kabul last week. "We denounce the executions and violations of human rights committed in Afghanistan," he said.
The summit was attended by the presidents of Kazakhastan Tajikistan, Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan as well as by Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin.

The summit was called to discuss possible steps if the Taleban continued to advance north to the southern borders of the Commonwealth of Independent States, a loose 12-member grouping formed as the Soviet Union collapsed in 1991.

Nazarbayev said that the participants at the summit would take "adequate measures" to defend themselves if the conflict spills over from Afghanistan. But he, and other participants, made clear no practical steps would be taken unless this happens.
